item.title: A Revenue Layer for CKB Nodes (1 posts)
item.description: Cheers for the mention @joshyates1980. @psawyerberlin yeah the finalization bot is a good example of what you mean. Release and refund are permissionless on CrowdCell, the lock script checks where the money goes so it doesn’t matter who submits the tx. Right now the bot runs next to the indexer on a free Render instance, which works but it’s still one operator. One detail that might help the design, the fee for release and refund already comes out of the pledge cell, so a runner doesn’t need to hold CKB for those, but there’s also nothing in it for them yet. item.title: Obscell Wallet: A Privacy-Preserving TUI Wallet for CKB (2 posts)
item.description: A related development worth sharing: Silent Payments (BIP352) is already usable on Bitcoin mainnet. Sparrow 2.5.0 added receiving support, including support for air-gapped hardware wallet signers. It works at the wallet layer using existing Taproot outputs, without requiring a new consensus upgrade. It follows the same general idea as stealth addresses: publish one reusable payment code, while each payment goes to a different on-chain address. The interesting difference is that Silent Payments derives the shared secret from transaction input keys, avoiding extra on-chain notification data. The tradeoff is more scanning work for the recipient. This could be a useful reference for Obscell’s...

item.title: Cellula.id: `.cell` names on CKB, with the contracts public and reproducible (1 posts)
item.description: @Jnr6 thanks, good to hear. Three things changed since the issue, for when you get to it: The contract upgrade landed on mainnet yesterday at 21:00 UTC. The code hashes are the same, so name cells verify as before; only the code cells moved. The new data hashes are in cells-contracts (docs/SECURITY.md) and the outpoints in cellula.id/api/verify. Names can now be held as deeds on mainnet (a Spore holds the name). The payout address still comes from the name’s records, so forward resolution in Send works the same. If a reference helps for your step 4, the same hint-then-verify checks are in cellula-sdk 0.2.0 (resolver.ts, MIT). Happy to help when you start.
